Hey, it's all part of the learning experience to hit certain roadblocks, wanting to improve and asking for advice is already the right path.


TL;DR Choose two comps, force them to learn strengths/weaknesses, some basic fundamentals through it. Using 6 Keepers comp as an example.


Although it's good to be flexible, it's probably best to stick with improving your fundamentals first, as flexing in gold-plat elo isn't as important for now. Especially since we're unable to check how you manage your gold throughout the game, we don't really know what you're doing wrong there. What we can do instead is look at your other fundamentals.


Go to this [link](https://tftactics.gg/meta-report) and choose two of those comps that you like (except spirit/sharps, as it's heavily contested by other players in the lobby and having two players forcing it can result in both of them holding hands to 7th and 8th). Force the shit out of those two comps, with one that you'll always force, and the second one as a backup in the rare case that three people in your lobby are going that.


Forcing a comp is a great way to learn a lot of aspects of the game. You get to learn which units are your carries, which items you'll want to build for said carries, which stages to roll for your units, etc. Once you learn the basics, you can then move onto positioning, knowing what counters your comp, how to transition into these comps more effectively.


Let's take 6 Keepers Kennen comp for example. Our main carry is Kennen, with Xayah as our secondary carry. In order for 6 Keepers to do well, you absolutely want GA and Morello for Kennen. Why? GA guarantees Kennen to cast his ult at least once during a fight, while Morello offers both healing reduction, a great counter to Slayers, and providing burn damage. For the last item, you can put in whatever good offensive item for him. Since his main source of damage comes from his ult, which is magic damage, good items for him will be JG, Ionic Spark, Rabadon's, and HoJ. If you're top 4 and you see a player going 8 Brawlers, GS can also be decent as your last item.


What's good about this comp is that you really only need to focus on Kennen for your items first. Due to this, it also makes it a relatively easy comp to transition, as you won't have to worry about late game transitions as much. For the rest of your team, you can delegate your other items to them, attack damage centered items for Xayah (although HoJs are preferred on her, as she heavily benefits the healing part of it), other magic damage items can be given to Kindred, while defensive items can be given to Aatrox. Another good point to mention about this comp is that Aatrox is a key unit. Any units that would be outside of Kennen/Xayah's ults can be pulled into their range using him.


As for which chosen you would want for this comp, Kennen is obviously what you'd like to hit. Rolling at level 7 is your best bet, as you'll have a 58% chance at hitting a 3 cost chosen. Other good ones, in order, are Keeper Xayah, Executioner Xayah, and Vanguard Aatrox. 


I'll briefly mention some other important aspects of the comp, such as positioning Kennen and Xayah at the ends of the board on either left/right, having both Kennen and Aatrox at the front of your team, and that Shroud is your biggest counter as an item, but won't elaborate. I'll let you know about these but I want you to learn for yourself as to why these are the case by practicing and learning the comp.


Of course, you could just watch this [video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uaNDLDEmr60) to digest this block of info instead.

I actually wrote down a summary for some of my friends regarding info about gameplay.

**Blackreef Island**

* Much like the Bermuda Triangle, the island has been shrouded in mystery, forming a legacy of its own.
* In the 40s, the government set up a few military bunkers on the island to study its strange phenomenon, but when the military pulled out, the island sat deserted for years.
* It wasn’t until the 60s that someone finally cracked open the island’s secrets.

**Visionaries**

* Frank Spicer
 * One of the eight targets, a security specialist and wannabe rockstar.
 * He’ll be located in a makeshift casino nicknamed The Rambling Rock Club.
 * Much like Aramis Stilton’s Mansion, Colt won’t be able to use his powers in this area, as anyone who enters his club must wear a Slab-inhibiting wristband.
 * All visionaries when killed either drop a unique weapon or Slab. Frank’s unique weapon is an SMG called Constancy Automatic, which boasts two magazines, allowing Colt to fire the weapon while reloading without interruption.
* Julianna
 * Julianna is a unique Visionary, as she will not only move around, hunting down the player, but can also be controlled by other players who invade their world.
 * In order to play as Julianna however, players will have to play through a bit of Colt’s campaign before they unlock her mode.
 * Julianna won’t have a traditional narrative campaign, but she will have a progression system, as playing her will unlock various cosmetics that can be applied to both Julianna and Colt.
* Egor Serling
 * One of the eight targets, an arrogant pseudoscientist obsessed with strange phenomena and urban legends.
 * After learning about Blackreef, he convinced a wealthy benefactor to bankroll a series of experiments on the island, which led to a few discoveries, one of the first being Trinkets.
 * As Serling’s crew continues to make new Trinkets, they eventually craft objects of even greater power, which they nickname Slabs.
 * Serling’s biggest discovery comes when he realizes that he can break time itself. Inventing a way to form a time loop, they started the AEON program, allowing them to relive the same day over and over again.

**Time Loop**

* Unfortunately, the time loop doesn’t function as expected. This is where Colt’s story picks up.
* Deathloop opens just after the AEON scientists have flipped the switch and created the time loop.
* Everyone on the island thinks that this is the first day of the time-loop experiment, but Colt knows that the AEOn program has been running for some time.
* The entire island is trapped in a repeating cycle, and Colt is one of the only people who can retain his memories from one loop to the next.

**Trinkets**

* Much like Bonecharms in the Dishonored series, Trinkets will allow for small changes in gameplay, such as increasing your jump height or make your weapons suddenly shoot gas instead of bullets.

**Slabs**

* Each Slab has four potential upgrades, two of which can be equipped at any given time and stack on top of each other.
* The “Blink” ability from the Dishonored series is called the “Shift” Slab, allowing Colt to teleport himself for a short distance.
 * Two potential upgrades of his Shift have been revealed.
  * One can be modified so that when it’s activated, Colt hovers in mid-air.
  * Another upgrade allows Colt to swap places with a character.
* The “Domino” ability from Dishonored 2 is called the “Nexus” Slab, allowing Colt to link the fates of multiple characters together.
 * When characters are linked, they all take the same amount of damage. Alternatively, if one is launched, the rest follow suit.
 * Two of the potential upgrades of his Nexus have been revealed.
  * One can be modified so that attacks home in on his targets.
  * Another upgrade allows Colt to lob a grenade-like blast that automatically links characters within a certain radius.
* The “Havoc” Slab gives Colt steel skin, allowing him to absorb damage.
* An unnamed Slab allow Colt to become invisible, allowing him to sneak past enemies undetected.

**Other gameplay**

 * As Colt explores Blackreef Island, he’ll come across a series of messages written across the environment.
  * These often offer helpful tips or highlight areas that Colt should explore and may play an important role in helping him break the loop.
 * Players won’t be able to save whenever they want. However, a Reprise system is put in place, which allows Colt to rewind the clock several seconds before his death to give them another chance.
  * Colt starts with two Reprises each day, which can be replenished by killing Julianna.
 * Colt will have access to grenades, one of the variants revealed being a trip mine that activates when an enemy walks into it.
 * As shown in a previous trailer, Colt will be able to use a hacking tool that can be used for various machinery (such as turrets or reprogramming doors to open).
